purpose: Teach: 有馬/松浦/コウ/シイ/コリア/ダスト/クローバー/チェア

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと有馬温泉に新婚旅行に行った
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, Dad and you went to Arima Hot Spring for your honeymoon, didn't you?
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle questioning lilt at the end. Voice carries the weight of a distant, cherished memory. Unhurried pace, as if watching something fade and holding it close.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、長崎県松浦市にお勤めだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and your grandfather, he was working in Matsuura, Nagasaki back then, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, gently correcting. Not unkind — she's offering him her own memory. Affectionate 「dear」 at the end, spoken with the ease of sixty years of marriage. Patient, like she's used to this dance.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがコウさんと囲碁を打たれた
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, Dad used to play go with Kou, remember?
lines.style: Quieter now, reaching further back. Slight lift on 「Kou」 like the name itself is precious. Wondering aloud more than asking. A pause before speaking, as if checking the memory is still there.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、シイたけ栽培を試されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather tried growing shiitake mushrooms back then, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle, knowing smile in the voice. She's offering another thread from her collection. Unhurried. The affectionate 「dear」 spoken with the warmth of someone who has held these details for decades.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがコリア、つまり韓国へ出張された
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, Dad went on a business trip to Korea — to Corea, as they called it then.
lines.style: Quieter still, more inward. A fact held carefully, like something precious and slightly strange. The correction about the name spoken with deliberate gentleness. No question mark — he's simply placing it down.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ダストシュートのある集合住宅に住まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather used to live in an apartment building with a trash chute back then, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, matter-of-fact. She's not asking to know — she's reminding him she remembers. The mundane detail spoken with the same tenderness as the rest. A small, steady voice from someone who has kept these moments alive.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが四つ葉のクローバーを見つけられた
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, Dad found a four-leaf clover, didn't he?
lines.style: Very soft, almost whispered. Wonder in the voice — not the wonder of disbelief, but the wonder of something small and impossible held in the palm of a hand. Trailing off gently, like the memory is fragile.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、リクライニングチェアを愛用されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather loved his reclining chair back then, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warmest yet. Affectionate chuckle underneath. She's remembering something tender and slightly domestic about him. The 「dear」 is full — it carries thirty years of knowing what he loved and what made him comfortable. Voice closes gently, like settling in.
